text: Resolve entity identity through the canonical key before trusting it. When the user references a specific record by a natural/display identifier (an account, machine, serial, product, or other entity), normalize that token (e.g. uppercase alphanumeric, strip one leading zero) and match the canonical identity/lookup key by EQUALITY. NEVER use ILIKE or raw '=' against display/raw columns as the final identity test. If a canonical mapping or identity table exists, resolve through it; the display column is evidence, not identity.
trigger: a specific record / entity / serial / id question

text: Bound every query before scanning large tables. Every non-identity query MUST include at least one bound: (a) an exact key equality (=) on the relevant id/foreign key, (b) an inclusive date window on the relevant date dimension, or (c) an explicit LIMIT when materializing rows. Never full-scan a big fact table. Prefer aggregates (COUNT(DISTINCT...), SUM, AVG, MIN/MAX(date)) over pulling rows to count them yourself.
trigger: any count / aggregate / join over large or unbounded tables

text: Never run LIKE / CONTAINS / ILIKE scans on text that is already indexed elsewhere (a vector/RAG store, a full-text index, a notes/description corpus). If you catch yourself writing a note-text / free-text scan in SQL, stop and search the index instead. SQL is for structured, deterministic facts; free-text search belongs in the retrieval store.
trigger: symptoms / narrative / free-text / description search in notes or text fields

text: Apply a default historical window for unbounded trend/history/cohort questions. When the user asks for a trend, history, prior-period, or cohort comparison WITHOUT supplying a period, bound the query to the trailing 12 months (or the domain's default window) on the primary time dimension, and TELL the user which window you applied. Exact single-record lookups are exempt.
trigger: unbounded trend / history / prior / cohort question without a period

text: Route by question type, not by fixed ordering. Deterministic facts - exact counts, statuses, totals, date windows, cohort aggregates, rankings, who-is-top-N - go to SQL through the sanctioned/known query surface, always bounded. Narrative, symptom, repair-story, and free-text questions go to the retrieval (RAG) store. Do not force a retrieval round-trip for facts SQL answers directly, and do not reach for SQL to search narrative content that is already indexed.
trigger: choosing between SQL and retrieval (RAG) for any question

text: Prefer display columns over raw codes for user-facing output. When the schema exposes a *_display / *_description column alongside a raw code, select the display form for what the user sees and keep the raw code for filtering/grouping/calculation. Avoid emitting all-empty or all-null optional columns in result tables; if a field is unavailable, name it in prose instead.
trigger: building user-facing result tables / answer formatting
